question: Organisms that reproduce strictly via asexual mechanisms are defined as a single biological species if they share similar structural features and genetic materials.

[TAXONOMIC ANALYSIS] Explain how phylogenetics differs from old classification approaches. Given that Organism X and Organism Y belong to the same Order, while Organism X and Organism Z belong to the same Class but different Orders, deduce which pair shares a more recent common ancestor.
rubric: To score full points, the comparative deduction must state: 1) Old classification systems were based on similarities in observable physical structural features. Modern phylogenetics relies on gene sequencing, assuming that greater similarities in genetic materials reflect closer evolutionary history. 2) Organism X and Organism Y share a more recent common ancestor because organisms belonging to the same lower taxonomic level (Order) are more closely related than those sharing only a higher level (Class).
